Two-way fixed-effects difference-in-differences

Source: R/did.R
did.Rd

Adds the indicator treated = 1(t >= first treated period) to the model and fits it with individual and time fixed effects (two-way fixed effects, TWFE). With a single treatment date (the canonical two-group, two-period design and its multi-period extension) the coefficient on treated is the average treatment effect on the treated under parallel trends. With staggered adoption and effects that vary over time or across cohorts the TWFE coefficient is a weighted average that can put negative weight on some effects (Goodman-Bacon 2021; de Chaisemartin and D'Haultfoeuille 2020): use eventstudy() to look at the dynamics and a heterogeneity-robust estimator (attgt() for Callaway and Sant'Anna 2021, or etwfe() for the extended TWFE of Wooldridge 2021, 2023) when adoption is staggered.

Usage

did(formula, data, index, treat, family = "gaussian", vcov = "cluster", ...)

Arguments

formula

outcome and control variables, e.g. y ~ age or y ~ 1; the treatment indicator is added

data

a data.frame in long format

index

c(individual, time); the time index must be numeric

treat

name of the column holding each individual's first treated period (in the units of the time index); NA, 0 or Inf for units that are never treated

family

"gaussian", "poisson", "negbin" or "binomial" (conditional logit, logit link only; see Details)

vcov

covariance type, cluster-robust by individual by default

...

further arguments passed to panglm()

Value

a panglm() fit whose coefficient treated is the DiD estimate (a log odds ratio for family = "binomial"), with a component did (number of treated and never-treated individuals, treatment cohorts). Its call is the did() call. All panglm() methods apply.

Details

The family can be Gaussian (effect on the mean), Poisson or negative binomial (effect on the log rate: exp(coef) is a ratio, and Poisson FE DiD needs only the conditional mean to be correct, Wooldridge 2023), or binomial for a binary outcome. The binomial model is the two-way conditional (Chamberlain) logit of panglm(): the individual effects are conditioned out exactly and the time effects enter as dummies inside the conditional likelihood, as in survival::clogit(y ~ treated + factor(time) + strata(id)). Its coefficient treated is then a log odds ratio, conditional on the individual effect (exp(coef) is the odds ratio), parallel trends is assumed on the log-odds scale, and individuals whose outcome never changes carry no information and are dropped. It is not an effect on the probability scale: for average effects on the treated in probability points use etwfe() with family = "binomial". Controls that do not vary within individuals are absorbed by the individual effects and dropped.

Validation

Numerical accuracy is checked in the package tests and in the validation suite; see the validation article on the package website.

References

Goodman-Bacon, A. (2021). Difference-in-differences with variation in treatment timing. Journal of Econometrics, 225, 254-277. doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2021.03.014

de Chaisemartin, C. and D'Haultfoeuille, X. (2020). Two-way fixed effects estimators with heterogeneous treatment effects. American Economic Review, 110, 2964-2996. doi:10.1257/aer.20181169

Wooldridge, J. M. (2023). Simple approaches to nonlinear difference-in-differences with panel data. The Econometrics Journal, 26, C31-C66. doi:10.1093/ectj/utad016

See also

summary.panglm() and the other panglm() methods for the fitted model.

Other policy evaluation: attgt(), etwfe(), eventstudy()

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- expand.grid(id = 1:200, year = 2015:2022)
d$first <- ifelse(d$id <= 100, 2019, NA)        # policy in 2019 for half
a <- rnorm(200)
d$visits <- 3 + a[d$id] + 0.1 * (d$year - 2015) +
  1.5 * (!is.na(d$first) & d$year >= d$first) + rnorm(nrow(d))
fit <- did(visits ~ 1, data = d, index = c("id", "year"), treat = "first")
summary(fit)
#> 
#> Call:
#> did(formula = visits ~ 1, data = d, index = c("id", "year"), 
#>     treat = "first")
#> 
#> Family: gaussian  Link: identity  Model: within  Effect: twoways 
#> N = 1600  groups = 200  vcov: cluster 
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#>         Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> treated  1.71437    0.09866   17.38   <2e-16 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Log-likelihood: -2221 
#> Dispersion parameter: 1.081 
#> Residual df: 1392  Iterations: 2
#> 
# binary outcome: conditional logit, the coefficient is a log odds ratio
d$admitted <- rbinom(nrow(d), 1, plogis(-1 + a[d$id] + 0.05 * (d$year - 2015) +
  0.8 * (!is.na(d$first) & d$year >= d$first)))
fitb <- did(admitted ~ 1, data = d, index = c("id", "year"), treat = "first",
            family = "binomial")
#> 16 group(s) with no within-group outcome variation dropped (all-0 or all-1) -- they carry no information for the conditional likelihood.
exp(coef(fitb))                                  # odds ratio
#>  treated 
#> 2.020067
